title: Compensating actions
description: Learn about compensating actions for rolling back distributed transactions. Understand how to design reliable undo operations for sagas.

data.text: Compensating actions are operations that undo the effects of a previous transaction. They're essential for sagas and other distributed transaction patterns to maintain consistency when operations fail.
In distributed systems, you can't rollback transactions across services like you can in a single database. Instead, you execute compensating actions that logically undo the previous operation.

items: Compensating actions are the opposite of the original operation
They don't need to restore the exact previous state
They just need to bring the system to a consistent state
Must be idempotent—may be called multiple times
Should be designed as part of the operation, not an afterthought

data.title: Not a Rollback
data.text: Compensating actions are not database rollbacks. They're business operations that logically undo the effect of a previous operation.

items.title: Reserve Hotel → Cancel Reservation
items.description: Original: Reserve room. Compensating: Cancel the reservation. May incur fees, but returns the room to available inventory.

items.title: Charge Credit Card → Refund
items.description: Original: Charge card. Compensating: Process refund. May take time and incur fees, but reverses the charge.

items.title: Ship Order → Return
items.description: Original: Ship product. Compensating: Initiate return. Doesn't undo the shipping, but handles the business consequence.

items.title: Send Email → Send Correction
items.description: Original: Send notification. Compensating: Send correction email. Can't undo the sent email, but can correct the information.

items: Idempotency—compensating actions must be safe to retry
Reliability—compensating actions should always succeed
Simplicity—keep compensating actions simple and reliable
Semantic correctness—bring system to consistent state
Side effects—document any side effects of compensation

data.title: Not Always Possible
data.text: Some operations can't be compensated (e.g., sending a physical letter). Design your system to minimize these or accept that compensation is incomplete.

items: Identifying what needs compensation
Designing the correct compensating action
Handling compensation failures
Managing the cost of compensation
Business acceptance of compensating behavior
Design compensating actions alongside the original operation
Make compensating actions idempotent by default
Test compensating actions thoroughly
Monitor compensation success and failure
Document the compensation strategy clearly
Consider the business impact of compensation

data.text: Compensating actions can fail. Have a strategy for handling compensation failures.

items: Retry the compensating action with backoff
Manual intervention for stubborn failures
Compensate manually and record the resolution
Accept the inconsistent state and document it
Implement alerting for compensation failures

data.title: Monitoring
data.text: Track compensation failures as high-priority incidents. Failed compensation means your system is in an inconsistent state.
